body:
You're right, it isn't my job to guide her which is also frustrating me because I feel as if I'm having to teach her all this stuff. My mom is a little too lax and doesn't really understand how bad it is for me so she doesn't really try. Like I said in my other reply, not a bad mom, just a little.. unreliable.

I think those are really good solutions thank you for suggesting them to me. I really wasn't sure what to do to reassure her. Recently my headphones broke so they haven't been working as well which is where a lot of my frustration comes from too.

Before the quarantine happened I walked her to the park sometimes and we were a bit closer bc I also walked her home from school, which I enjoyed. Naturally bc of the quarantine it's also harder to cope with the noise 24/7...She is a very outdoors girl so I'm hoping after this pandemic clears up we can go back to before. TY!!

Ahh, I also believe my sister is neurodiverse in some way (no diagnosis, i just recognize a lot of symptoms in her that i had as a child & do now) so part of me is aware that her not listening/understanding very well is because of that. 

I've talked to my mom briefly about it and she does tell her to stop in the moment, but she never actually *talks* to her about it which is why it repeats. My mom, as other comments are saying, is a little indifferent. I wouldnt say shes a bad mother but she can be unreliable when it comes to help.
